Subject: An Update on Your Brewlog Pre-Order

Dear Brewer,

First of all, thank you. Your support has made Brewlog possible, and we're humbled that 640 of you have placed your trust in us.

We want to be upfront with you: because of delays in our Bluetooth certification process, shipping will now begin on March 17 instead of March 3. We know you're eager to start brewing, and we apologize for the inconvenience.

Our team is working hard to deliver a product that lives up to your expectations. Quality is our top priority, and it always will be.

If you'd rather cancel, just reply to this email and we'll issue a full refund, no questions asked.

Cheers to great beer,
Niamh Doyle
Founder, Brewlog

Subject: Halftone Is Now a Lightroom Plugin

Hi,

I shot weddings for years. I also spent whole evenings culling thousands of frames when I wanted to be editing, or sleeping. So I built Halftone.

As of today, February 2, it runs as a Lightroom Classic plugin. The AI flags blinks, blur, and near-duplicates without pulling you out of your workflow.

In our testing, it culled 3,000 photos in 6 minutes on an M2 MacBook Air.

Try it free for 7 days. After that, $15/month.

Get your evenings back.
Leo Martins
Founder, Halftone

Subject: Predictive Maintenance, Now in Your Hands — Introducing the Ferrous Self-Install Kit

Dear Plant Leader,

When a CNC machine goes down without warning, you lose more than hours. You lose the schedule you promised your customer.

That's the problem we built the Ferrous Self-Install Kit to solve. Each kit comes with 4 advanced vibration sensors and a smart gateway. Your own technician can install it in under 2 hours. No PLC changes. No disruption. No headaches.

We build it in Pune, for Indian manufacturers. The kit costs ₹1,20,000, plus a dashboard subscription of ₹6,000 per machine per month.

Your machines are already telling you when they're about to fail. Start listening.

Request your kit today.

Regards,
Aditi Kulkarni
CEO, Ferrous

Subject: Faster month-end close for Halberd

Hi Priya,

I came across Halberd Logistics and saw your recent move to NetSuite last year. Congratulations on that.

I also noticed you're hiring 2 accounts payable clerks, which suggests your finance team is scaling. That usually means more manual work, more spreadsheets, and longer month-ends.

Ledgerline is an AI-powered platform that matches bank and card transactions to NetSuite, so finance leaders can close faster and spend time on higher-value work. Our 38 customers have cut their close from 9 days to 4 on average.

Would you be open to a 20-minute call next week to see if we could do something similar for Halberd?

Best regards,
Erik Lund
Founder, Ledgerline

I saw that you currently sell through Instagram DMs. That works well for connecting with customers, but it gets harder to manage as the brand grows.

Would you like to see those two skincare stores for inspiration?

Warm regards,
Wanjiru Kamau
Founder, Fernway Studio

Subject: Kopa opens to every Kenyan freelancer on March 4

Habari,

We spent the beta with 2,000 freelancers fixing one problem: getting paid. Now you can build a professional invoice in seconds and your client pays you straight to M-Pesa. No chasing. No awkward "just checking in" messages.

You did the work. Get paid for it. Send your first invoice today.

Co-founder, Kopa

Pokoik is coming to Kraków.

From November 20, you can book 35 handpicked apartments in Kazimierz and Podgórze. Cobblestone streets, cafés on every corner, and plenty of creative energy. A good place for your next stay.

Your Kraków story starts here: pokoik.pl/krakow

Subject: Recovering lost billable hours at Kestrel & Finch

Hi Sophie,

I've been following Kestrel & Finch's growth, and I saw you're hiring a project manager. Congratulations on the expansion.

As your 34-person team scales, accurate time tracking matters more than ever. Many agencies lose significant revenue to incomplete timesheets without realizing it.

That's where Tabwise comes in. It pulls data from Google Calendar and Jira and fills in timesheets automatically, so there's no manual entry. Across 22 agencies, we've helped teams recover an average of 3.2 billable hours per person, per week. For a team your size, that adds up quickly.

Would you be open to a brief 15-minute chat to see if this fits?

Best,
Olu Adeyemi
Co-founder, Tabwise

Subject: Brightwater's new office and keeping noise down

Hi Jenna,

Congratulations on Brightwater Legal's move in February. A new office is a good chance to rethink how your team works and set up a space that supports focus, privacy, and productivity.

Confidential conversations are part of daily life at a law firm, and that's why many firms have turned to Quietroom. Our soundproof phone booths reduce noise by 32 dB, assemble in 45 minutes, and start at $6,400, which makes them a flexible investment for the new space.

I'd be glad to send our spec sheet along with a floor-plan template so you can see how the booths might fit in.

Would that be helpful?

Best,
Mark Hollis

Subject: Your Post on CI and Flaky Tests

Hi Dmitri,

I just read your blog post, Why our CI takes 40 minutes. The part about roughly a third of your reruns being caused by flaky tests stood out. It's a problem many engineering teams deal with and few talk about openly.

At Patchwork CI, we built a platform that automatically detects and quarantines flaky tests in GitHub Actions, so teams can spend less time on reruns and ship with confidence. We're already trusted on 1,200 repositories worldwide.

I'd like to offer you a free run on one of your repos, no strings attached, and share what we find.

Would that be of interest?

Cheers,
Tomas

Subject: Never Sell Out Again, Hollow Oak

Hi Grace,

I saw your Instagram post about last year's holiday line selling out in 9 days. Great problem to have, but it means candles people wanted never made it to a cart.

The holidays are coming again. This time you can see it coming.

Right now you run shifts across 22 outlets. Add 5 more and scheduling gets harder fast. That is the problem we built Rotaship to solve.

Rotaship runs inside WhatsApp. Your staff view and swap shifts themselves, so managers stop chasing schedules by hand. 140 outlets already use it this way.

Do you have 20 minutes for a call? I would like to show you how it fits Sate Pak Ujang.

Dewi Santoso
Co-founder, Rotaship

Hi Marcus,

Think about what you could do with those three weeks back, and with time freed up for higher-impact work.

I'd like to process one of your interviews for free so you can see the results yourself. Would you be open to that?

Best,
Hana Lee

Subject: Your grant could pay for a Coldframe

Dear Tom,

Congratulations on the energy-efficiency grant. Good to see Ashby Growers spending it on something that lasts.

Founder, Coldframe

Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

Let me explain.

5 months in, they walked away. It stung. A lot.

But failure isn't the opposite of success. It's part of it.

The reason they left: they had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we did what good teams do. We listened. We learned. We built.

We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. That changed how we think about our customers, not just our product.

Today, we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

The lesson? Your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough.

Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build. You just have to listen.

What's a loss that shaped your company?

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would stay free for open source. People told us we were crazy. How would we make money, they asked.

Today we run on 1,200 repositories. Around 900 of them are open source.

But here's what got me. Across those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test.

One in seven. Countless hours of your time, burned on red builds that were never real failures.

Open source gave us more than users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers. We shipped it on November 12.

Giving back is not charity. It is strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

1,000 families.

14 months ago, Pebble Pantry was an idea I scribbled down on maternity leave. Sleep-deprived, staring at an empty fridge at 7pm.

Today, 1,000 families pay €4.99 a month to make dinner time a little easier.

Here's the part I love: no ad campaigns, no growth hacks. Most families found us through school WhatsApp groups. Parents telling other parents.

That's not growth. That's trust.

To every mum and dad who shared us in a group chat: thank you. You built this with us.

To every founder on a shoestring: keep going. Your community is your superpower.

#Startups #Portugal #Parenting #FemaleFounders #Gratitude

We built an app we loved. Almost nobody used it.

When we launched Rotaship, the mobile app looked sharp. We figured restaurant staff would pick it up fast.

They didn't. Only 12% of staff opened it in the first month.

That stung, but it taught us something. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding to it.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They already live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025 we killed the app and moved everything into WhatsApp.

It worked. 140 outlets now use it, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

If you're building for busy people, build where they already are. Don't ask them to come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

We're hiring our first Account Executive.

That's the news. Here's why it matters.

So far we've sold 210 booths. Every single one sold by a founder. That worked for a while, but we can't be in every meeting forever. So we're hiring someone to sell with us.

Maybe that's you.

You'd need to actually like selling. Not tolerate it, like it. You'd need to keep your head when things move fast, because they will. And you'd need to be good with people, because this job is mostly people.

What you get:

£55,000 base, plus commission.
Our London office, 3 days a week.
A real say in what workplace focus looks like, because we're building it now.

If that sounds like your kind of job, apply through the link in the comments. One person gets this role. It might as well be you.

#Hiring #SalesJobs #London #StartupJobs #JoinOurTeam

After 11 years in a clinic, I quit. Here's why.

I always loved being a vet. But something kept breaking my heart.

Day after day, I saw anxious pets so terrified that we had to sedate them just to examine them.

I knew there had to be a better way.

So in 2023, I took the leap and founded Doorstep Vet.

The idea was simple: bring high-quality, compassionate care to pets in the one place they feel safest, their own home.

Today, our team of 4 vets does around 30 home visits a week. Every single one reminds me why we do this.

Calmer pets. Happier owners. Better medicine.

Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is follow your heart.

#Veterinary #PetCare #Melbourne #Entrepreneurship #FollowYourPassion

Why we stopped billing by the hour — and never looked back.

When we started Fernway Studio, we did what every agency does: we charged hourly.

The result was that 4 of our first 6 projects went over budget.

Clients were frustrated. We were frustrated. Trust was eroding.

So in 2024, we made a bold decision. We switched to a fixed price: KES 450,000 per Shopify store. Period.

And it changed everything.

Clients know exactly what they're paying. We're incentivized to work smarter, not longer. Relationships are built on trust, not timesheets.

Since then, we've launched 31 stores. Only 2 went over our 6-week timeline.

Pricing isn't just a number. It's a promise.

Founders, how do you price your services? Let me know in the comments!

#Entrepreneurship #Africa #Shopify #AgencyLife #Pricing

Hardware is hard. Here's our story.

Our first production run at Shelfwise didn't go as planned.

400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact.

As a young hardware startup, it would have been easy to cut corners. But that's not who we are.

We decided to recall and replace every one of those 400 labels, at our own cost. It set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%.

Because trust is everything.

We didn't stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, we've had zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

Mistakes don't define you. How you respond to them does.

To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.

#Hardware #Startups #Manufacturing #Leadership #Integrity

We raised our prices by 50%. Here's what happened.

In September, we made one of the scariest calls in Tabwise's history: $8 to $12 per user per month.

Why? Our support costs per customer had doubled since launch. So we had a choice. Cut quality, or charge what the product is actually worth.

We charged what it's worth.

Still, we didn't want to punish the people who got us here. Every existing customer kept their $8 price for 12 months.

The result?

2 out of 140 customers churned in the following 2 months.

Two.

Here's the lesson: your customers don't pay for software. They pay for outcomes. Price accordingly.

Founders, when did you last raise your prices?

#SaaS #Pricing #StartupLessons #Growth #B2B

2,000 freelancers. KES 84 million. One mission.

When we started Kopa, we had a simple dream: help Kenyan freelancers get paid fairly and on time.

Today I'm proud to share that 2,000 freelancers have joined our private beta, and together they've sent invoices worth KES 84 million.

That number means rent paid, school fees covered, and dreams funded.

We also listened closely to your feedback. The #1 request was invoices in US dollars, and we heard you: it's officially on our roadmap.

And now the big news: our public beta opens March 4, so every freelancer can experience getting paid via M-Pesa.

The future of work is here, and it's African.

#Fintech #Kenya #Freelancing #MPesa #AfricanTech

$50K MRR. Bootstrapped. 18 months.

I still can't believe I'm typing this.

When I started Crateful, people told me I needed VC funding. That I'd never compete without a big team. That bootstrapping was "too slow."

Well. Here we are.

$50,000 in monthly recurring revenue. Zero outside funding. A team of 3.

Our secret weapon? The Shopify App Store. About 60% of our signups come from there. Be where your customers are already looking.

So if you're a bootstrapped founder grinding late at night: your path is valid. Profitability beats hype. Sustainability beats vanity metrics.

Now tell me. What's one thing that helped you grow without funding? Drop it below.

#Bootstrapped #SaaS #Shopify #IndieHackers #FounderJourney

3 days. That is how long one spindle failure shut down our line.

Years ago, I worked as a maintenance engineer at an auto-parts plant in Pune. One day a spindle failed, and an entire production line sat idle for 3 long days.

The part that still bothers me is this: the warning signs were there. 2 weeks earlier, vibration readings had clearly shown the problem. No one was watching.

That moment changed everything for me. In 2022, I founded Ferrous with one mission: to make sure no manufacturer ever has to experience that kind of preventable downtime again.

Today, our sensors are on 410 machines across 17 plants.

Every reading is a story. Every alert is a breakdown avoided. Every plant is a step closer to the future of Indian manufacturing.

Data only matters if someone is listening.

#Manufacturing #Industry40 #PredictiveMaintenance #MakeInIndia #StartupStory

100 rooftops. 100 businesses. 100 reasons to celebrate.

Today marks a big milestone for Gridline Solar: we have officially completed our 100th installation.

And it is a special one, a hardworking mechanic's workshop in the heart of Mooca.

Just 2 years ago, we installed our very first system. Since then, we have helped 100 small businesses across São Paulo switch to clean energy, every single one with R$ 0 upfront.

We promised installation in 21 days. Our average is 19.

This is about more than solar panels. It is about supporting local businesses, strengthening our communities, and building a brighter future for Brazil.

Thank you to our team and to every customer who believed in us.

Here's to the next 100.

#Solar #CleanEnergy #SãoPaulo #SmallBusiness #Sustainability

Why we dropped the 25% recruiting fee.

For years, Northbound Talent charged what every recruiting firm charges: 25% of first-year salary.

It never sat right with me.

Our average fee ran about $41,000 per hire. For an early-stage startup, that burns serious runway. And the incentives were wrong. Higher salary, bigger fee. Is that partnership?

So in January we went flat: $18,000 per hire. No percentages. No games.

Since then we've placed 26 senior Rust engineers, and our client relationships have never been stronger.

The recruiting industry needs to catch up. Founders deserve better.

Would you work with a flat-fee recruiter? Tell me.

#Recruiting #Startups #RustLang #Hiring #FutureOfWork

4 countries. 14 people. 1 team.

Building a remote team isn't easy, but it's worth it.

At Linguo Labs, our team of 14 spans Estonia, Latvia, Finland, and Sweden. And we've never felt more connected.

What works for us:

Written-first culture: Most of our work is written and reviewed asynchronously, so everyone can do deep, focused work on their own schedule.

No-Meeting Wednesdays: One full day each week to focus, create, and recharge.

In-person twice a year: We all come together in Tallinn to connect, celebrate, and plan ahead.

Remote work is really about how you work together, wherever you are.

What's your best tip for building a remote culture?

640 pre-orders.

brewlog.co
